items.title: Live: Tropical Cyclone Narelle forecast to make landfall as category four
items.description: Tropical Cyclone Narelle is forecast to start to make landfall in Far North Queensland this morning. Follow live.

items.title: Live: Iran vows 'zero restraint' if oil sites hit, Trump says US won't send ground troops
items.description: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth could not give "a definitive timeframe" for when the war would end, adding the Pentagon will seek more money from Congress. Follow live.

items.title: Swap your super to cash or ride out the market ructions? The experts weigh in
items.description: Experts are urging Australians to stay calm and weather the storm as the effects of the war in the Middle East reverberate through financial markets.

items.title: Government explores new tax for gas, coal to buffer fuel costs
items.description: The prime minister's department has requested options to impose a new tax on gas giants as a buffer to shield Australians from the economic shock of the Middle East war.

items.title: Iranian government official levels series of allegations at Australia, US and Israel
items.description: One of Iran's deputy foreign ministers, Esmaeil Baghaei, accuses the US of "terrorist acts" and issues a warning to Australia about being on the wrong side of history.

items.title: Iranians brace for Australia's new laws stopping temporary migrants
items.description: Migrants and human rights advocates say new laws stopping temporary migration from designated countries will keep families apart and make Australia's immigration system less predictable and fair.

items.title: Budget repair and cost-of-living relief are at odds with each other
items.description: If the treasurer is serious about budget repair the government has to avoid the inevitable pressure for more cost-of-living relief which will only grow as many families' budgets become unmanageable.

items.title: Why your Uber and food delivery could get more expensive
items.description: Rideshare and delivery platforms face mounting pressure to bump up rates for drivers as they struggle with skyrocketing fuel prices.

items.title: Danish royals finish Australia tour with day in Hobart
items.description: King Frederik of Denmark and Queen Mary have been welcomed to Hobart by a crowd happy to see the Danish Royals up close.

items.title: Suburban hobby shops turn international arms dealers of drone age
items.description: You can't buy a tank at a car dealership or a jet fighter at duty free, but in 2026 you can get a small missile at a hobby shop. What's going on?

items.title: 'That's not very lady-like': Teen adds to family's wood-chopping legacy
items.description: Like her father, grandfather and great grandfather before her, woodchopping is part of Kallie's family legacy.

items.title: Great Gunston gets Hawks home at the MCG
items.description: Hawthorn finishes over the top of an understrength Sydney side to knock off the ladder-leaders at the MCG, thanks to a four-goal haul from Jack Gunston.

items.title: Dogs hold on to down Canberra in brutal wet-weather battle
items.description: It was far from easy, but Canterbury have held on for a narrow win over the Raiders in torrential conditions in Canberra.

items.title: China cracks down on fentanyl networks after Trump delays Xi meeting
items.description: The country is one of the world’s highest producers of the chemicals used to produce the synthetic opioid in America.

items.title: BTS returns from military service. Is its comeback worth the wait?
items.description: K-pop supergroup BTS makes a comeback from mandatory military service today with a new album, concert and documentary. Here's why that's a big deal.

items.title: Weekly news quiz: History-making Oscars moments, a royal visit and fans storm the NRL field
items.description: It's been a big week in the news. Did you catch these stories?

items.title: How award-winning pianist Andrea Lam overcame stage fright
items.description: She made her debut with Sydney Symphony Orchestra at 13, but don't call Andrea Lam a piano prodigy. The award-winning pianist shares how she's kept kicking career goals without losing her love of the music.

items.title: Why would Iranian players decline asylum?
items.description: Seven Iranian footballers sought asylum in Australia after the Asian Cup. Within days, five chose to return to Iran. While officials say it was their decision, human rights groups point to pressure on their families back home. Reporting by Nicholas Maher for ABC News Loop.

items.title: Gold-tier health policies set to rise by as much as 25pc next month
items.description: Some Australians with private health insurance will face premium increases of as much as 25 per cent from next month, according to new analysis from CHOICE.

items.title: As UK battles 'unprecedented' outbreak of meningitis, Australia is unprepared
items.description: A growing outbreak of meningococcal B and meningitis has killed two young people in the UK as the number of infections climb. Here's why infectious disease professor Paul Griffin thinks Australia should be worried.

items.title: Family seeks DNA testing after news of Royal North Shore IVF mix-up
items.description: A family is pursuing DNA testing after hearing about an IVF mix-up at the same Sydney fertility clinic used to conceive its baby.

items.title: Bradley Murdoch provided with 'high level' of attention in prison, inquest told
items.description: Bradley Murdoch took the location of his victim Peter Falconio's remains to his grave. A coronial inquest has revealed police made two desperate attempts to get answers just days before he died.

items.title: Bondi lifeguard-turned-police officer makes dramatic surf rescue at Byron Bay
items.description: A former Bondi Rescue reality TV lifeguard who now works as a police officer in Byron Bay jumped into the surf to rescue three French tourists off a rocky headland.

items.title: Island council considers total ban on all new pet cats
items.description: Kangaroo Island Council is considering banning the introduction of all cats to the island, in a move the mayor is calling the "last cat policy". If successful, the ban would make the South Australian island one of the world's biggest inhabited islands to be free of cats.

items.title: Australia Zoo, government silent in search for captured totemic crocodile
items.description: Missing: One 80-year-old, 4.5 metre totemic crocodile. Last known whereabouts: Australia Zoo. Welcome to the fight for Old Faithful.
